poster.note: A strong stage poster: 'a droplet faces the Eclipse' reads at 685x343 and 90x70, and it sits dark and distinct on the wall (L 0.121). The 2:3 and 1:1 are recomposed, not cropped. Polish only: the crest is a flat grey cone, and the brightest rim flare is on the droplet's right, away from the Eclipse. The pink/cyan dust could be thinned so the four inks lead.

focus.note: 0.60,0.50 sits on the droplet's eyes. The eyes and body hold from the 577x163 strip to the 140x305 column, and in the 4:3 phone crop. The strip trims the crest and the lower body, which can't be avoided at 3.5:1.

icon.note: Drawn for 46: head, enlarged eyes and the cyan crest on violet night. Reads at 1x on night and on linen and is not a generic blob.

emblem.note: A separate tighter render with fewer parts (no crest). The eyes still read at 30 px on both grounds.

chip.note: More parts than the icon (the droplet plus a small Eclipse) and fewer than the poster. Reads at 64 px on both grounds.

keyStill.note: Real tension: a ring of glowing iron moths closes on the droplet, centred. It reads at 360x176 and at 132x66, in the poster's finish.

result.note: The payoff doesn't read: the Bell's shards look like loose grey pyramids, and the droplet is about 100 px tall in the 352 px band, so behind the headline it is just 'a droplet on a planet'. Bring the camera in so the falling Bell and the colour-flood ring are the subject of the middle 720x352 (must: the game's payoff moment).

gallery.note: Six real build moments in a telling order (loop, grown body, place, world-heart, glide, star finale), all different places and scales, each inside its central 4:3, with no added text. 03 is a place shot where the droplet is only findable at large sizes, which is acceptable for its job.

seals.note: Ten moments (9 proposed plus the event), each with three states. The round/hex/corona outlines are distinct at 32 px, with no gold, padlock or text. Earned and in-progress are close at 32 px on night, and the 'star' glyph loses its ray ring at that size, so widen the state step if time allows.

store.note: Five looks-only items, worn or shown as themselves, on Nacre's ground. Each is distinct at 40 px and in greyscale, with dark top corners and no gold or rarity glow.

owned.note: The verb 'absorbed' is the world's own: a pearl bead lands in the lower-left and closes with the droplet's crest, in about 800 ms, ending on the held frame. At 40 px the held frame is only a white dot; enough, but a slightly larger seal would help.

passTile.note: The droplet under Nacre's sky rings, on the world's ground, with no price. It is left unlettered (allowed) and reads from 169 down to 40 px.

passGrounds.note: Free (bare night), pass (pearl horizon) and bug.pass (a dimmed Eclipse corona) differ clearly, with no lettering and no guarded fills.

marker.note: A matter gem (next) and a pearl ring (held): world objects drawn for 48, and nothing that counts. The 'next' gem washes out on linen; check it on the light rail.

passRewards.note: Six rewards at full art, the tier shown by the row ground and never by a veil. All read at about 120 px; pearl-crest is the weakest, as an off-centre close-up.

update.note: One real change, the Chimera metamorphosis (halo and crest arriving, a ring of light), as a close-up in the poster's medium. It reads at 104x52, with no version number, date or NEW.

event.note: Lantern Night doesn't read as a special night: the pearl film lights Nacre's cap and limb across the whole right half, so there is no visible pool of light around the droplet, and the droplet is a small 50 px shape near the top edge. Darken the world outside a clear lantern pool and bring the droplet larger and lower into the right 55% (must: the world on a special day or night; the subject in the right 55%).

living.note: The held and reduced-motion frame matches the poster, and the module has the idle, react, enter, 6 s loop, squeezed, throwable bead and anchor behaviours. The light band stays dark in every mode. Frame time is about 0.3-1.1 ms on GPU but about 4 ms under software raster for enter and loop, over the ~2 ms budget. Checked from the code and the chat's harness captures; I did not re-run the harness.

backdrop.note: Ferrum at rest, one light, a hard horizon and a floor scene, with desktop and phone composed separately. The poster leads over it. On phone the dusky floor runs to the bottom, under Continue (about 3.5:1 contrast); end the floor higher or let it fall to night there.

share.note: A fresh render in the poster's register, with the droplet at 0.73 and the title in the plain left 43%. It matches the wall at 270 px, with no ember and no names.

phone.note: Recomposed for 9:16 (Eclipse above, droplet below), with the same one image, register and light band as the 2:1.

lockup.note: Iridescent capitals with a stated 120 px minimum (19 px letters). It is set in the face from the game's published cover, not the in-game Tilt Prism, so re-set it when the font arrives so the page and the game match.

overall: A coherent, fresh pass that reads unmistakably as Perlune: one chrome droplet, one night and one finish, almost all rendered by the game itself. The poster, gallery, marks and moving poster are ready. Two pictures need another pass: the result picture's payoff and the event banner's lantern pool are not legible at the sizes the page shows.
copying: none: nothing from the Threadbare, Carbon, Gob, Typos or Nightswim notYours lists appears. The violet and magenta are Perlune's own palette (the Eclipse and its dust), not Threadbare's crystal and heart.
made: Mostly rendered by the game's own WebGL2 renderer: the shipped build driven headless (Chromium/SwiftShader) with posed cameras and the game's own functions to stage real moments. The proposed store and pass looks were swapped in at render time through hooks. Seals were drawn in Python/numpy with a port of the game's shader material maths. The owned mark and the moving poster are Canvas 2D code porting the game's maths. The lockup was set in PIL.
